Messages.Body:
1. Can you use more than one damage prevention card against the same
attack?

EG: I am hit for a tonne of damage from Death of My Conscience. Can
I play more than one unflinching persistence, or a combination of
several fortitude cards and things like sideslip (ADV) to prevent all
the damage, or am I stuck only being able to prevent with one card?

2. With the Waste Management Operation, I assume I can take any card
from my ash heap, not just the top one, and stick it in the bottom of
my deck, right?

3. My vampire's opponent has two blood, and I play a blur, gaining 2
additional strikes. If I send the vampire into torpor with the first
strike, can I use the second strike to inflict agg, thus burning the
vampire, or is the second strike wasted?

4. If your vampire's hand damage is aggravated, does he or she have
the option of striking with non-agg damage? IE Can Thetmes use just
regular damage instead of agg?

5. What are the opinions of people on card limits? I personally
think that playing with more than 4 of any type of card, while being
more able to create theme decks, creates a situation along the lines
of a gambler with $5 to his name playing against another with $200.
Briefcase players will always walk away with the game because of a
single card combo that gets used 20 times, whereas the starting player
is stuck with a bunch of cards that are nice, but not overpowering.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
umur...@cc.umanitoba.ca wrote:
>
> 1. Can you use more than one damage prevention card against the same
> attack?

Yes.

> EG: I am hit for a tonne of damage from Death of My Conscience. Can
> I play more than one unflinching persistence, or a combination of
> several fortitude cards and things like sideslip (ADV) to prevent all
> the damage, or am I stuck only being able to prevent with one card?

Multiples are fine, even of the same card (except where card text limits
the use of the same card, as in Sideslip's case).

> 2. With the Waste Management Operation, I assume I can take any card
> from my ash heap, not just the top one, and stick it in the bottom of
> my deck, right?

Yes. The ash heap is unordered - there is no "top" or "bottom" to it as
far as the game is concerned.

> 3. My vampire's opponent has two blood, and I play a blur, gaining 2
> additional strikes. If I send the vampire into torpor with the first
> strike, can I use the second strike to inflict agg, thus burning the
> vampire, or is the second strike wasted?

Wasted, since combat ends as soon as one (or both) of the combatants is
no longer ready.

> 4. If your vampire's hand damage is aggravated, does he or she have
> the option of striking with non-agg damage? IE Can Thetmes use just
> regular damage instead of agg?

If he can find some non-hand strike, sure.
If he strikes with his hands, though, the damage he does will be agg.
If he strikes with a Bastard Sword, the damage will not be agg from his
special, since his special only makes the damage from his hand strikes
agg.

> 5. What are the opinions of people on card limits? I personally
> think that playing with more than 4 of any type of card, while being
> more able to create theme decks, creates a situation along the lines
> of a gambler with $5 to his name playing against another with $200.
> Briefcase players will always walk away with the game because of a
> single card combo that gets used 20 times, whereas the starting player
> is stuck with a bunch of cards that are nice, but not overpowering.

Not true. The gambling parallel has almost no base to argue against.
Card Limits in a game designed for no card limits from the ground up
(as VTES) are superfluous at best. In the specific case of V:TES, a CL
actually *favors* the "gambler with $200", since if he'll be able to
substitute cards more easily - using, for example, 4 Legal Manips and
4 Intimidations instead of his 8 Legal Manipulations if the CL is 4,
whereas the "gambler with $5" doesn't have access to 4 Intimidations
and is stuck with just 4 Legal Manips and, say, 4 Social Charms.
(Better examples of rare cards that closely mimic commons can be found,
but that example should suffice for illustration).

--

Time for you to shift your metagame. When people get untap/intercept

people that intercept is not always such a fun thing.

Eventually your metagame will settle into "totally random" mode, where
nobody even bothers trying to guess what everyone else will bring, and
so your odds ARE low that you'll sit next to two intercept decks...
since intercept decks are difficult to win with, and the assumption is

That's the Ventrue Law Firm's weakness, though. Intercept. If it
didn't have this problem, it would steamroll damn near everything; it
can pass ALL its votes 100% of the time with Presence and inherent
titles, it can countervote anything it feels like with Kindred
Coercion/Elder Kindred Network, it can survive combat with
Majesty/Skin of Steel, it handles bleed with Plain Old Deflection, and
it can pool gain via Minion Tap/5th/Voter Cap, or via Cons.
Boon/whatever.

So no, I don't see there being a need for such a card.

As far as needing rares to make it happen... pfft. OK, so you make a
KRC unblockable with Day Op. Great. Now you have someone in torpor,
who has to be rescued somehow, ... oops, wait, intercept works against
rescue actions too. d'oh! One copy of Day Op is sufficient. Dawn Op
is a two-edged sword and untidy. Hostile Takeover is neat, but far
from necessary.

In message <3AC210A5...@aon.at>, Thomas Pichler
<tom.p...@aon.at> writes

>Anyway, Derek's reply pretty much proves that apparently what really
>matters is local style of play - so all I can do is say, "please, come
>up with some common, affordable cards that make (cheap) Ventrue
>political playable in a heavy intercept environment, too".

Why?

Every deck needs a hole that can be exploited. For example, a focused
stealth bleed deck falls down on combat defence.

A Ventrue Political deck can pass lots of votes. If you want to stop
yourself dying from intercept, you either have to add stealth (so, use
big vampires like Arika and Queen Anne with Obfuscate), or mix and match
(the "Star Chamber" deck concept - some vampires with Obfuscate call
critical actions (say, Malkavians) but your Ventrue make the useful
votes pass (titles etc.)). If it's dying from combat, it needs to water
down the politics for some combat defence.

That's why V:TES has an upper deck limit. No deck can or should be able
to do everything. If a deck can do everything (e.g. bypass a heavy
intercept environment regardless), it's too powerful.

In a heavy intercept environment, you have a number of options.

If you're mad (e.g. like Legbiter), there's the Betrayer deck. Since it
focuses around so few actions, intercept can often be irrelevant. (The
hole here is that defence on the deck's part can be difficult.)

Decks that don't care about being blocked are also possible. Weenie
hordes don't care about being blocked, they'll get through eventually.
Throw in Computer Hacking and Laptop for bleed, Leather Jacket for
defence etc. You can even try weenie vote if you think you've got the
cards for it.

A deck that can bypass combat. Something like Form of Mist can continue
your action for you once you've been blocked, wasting that blocker's
intercept. Or you can use (superior) Freak Drive and (superior) Majesty
to take more actions, though watch out for the No Repeat Actions rule if
you play with it (basically, if you get blocked on a vote action, you
have to switch to something else - say a bleed action). This can work
well in a Ventrue vote deck, with some bleed on the side (some Govern
the Unaligned for flexibility on pool gain and bleed, say), or the other
way around. Majesty is also useful (though not totally effective)
combat defence.

A rush deck can help lots. So, they block you. They can't block you if
they're in torpor. Then you can waltz in and bleed them at your
leisure. Intercept decks tend to focus around mid-range to high-range
vampires. A good weenie rush deck can have double the number of
vampires, torporising their vampires as necessary - generally, left,
right and centre.

Trying to do everything is kind of like saying "Can I have a card that
lets my bleed deck ignore my prey's Deflections?" The defence is an
integral part of the game. If you haven't got the right offence, you
will and should come unstuck.

permanent +1 intercept bonuses such as verious retainers, Sport Bikes, Guardian

about 8 of every card.

because of the threat of high bleeds, secondly because people will expect I hit
them with stealth, anyway), and instead of stealth I can use
Disguised/Concealed Weapons (with a voluntary 8 card limit, that'd be 16, which
should suffice).

Does anybody have what they consider a better idea? [Imposing a 8/3/1 C/U/R

>get blocked [nobody blocks Gangrel or Tzimisce going on a bleed for 1,
>normally].

Take a combo of Brujah and !Brujah, drop in a big pile of Potence and
Celerity. Wasting 20 minutes with ELDB produces the following for me:

Crypt: (11 cards) [Min: 14, Max: 25, Avg: 4.82]
1 Anvil (dom CEL POT pre tha, Brujah, 6, Primogen)
1 Beast (ani cel OBF POT, Nosferatu Antitribu, 7)
1 Bianca (CEL pot pre, Brujah, 6)
1 Black Cat (CEL pot pre, Brujah, 5)

1 Sela (cel obt POT PRE, Brujah Antitribu, 6, Bishop)
1 Victor Tolliver (CEL pot, Brujah Antitribu, 4)
1 Yuri (cel pot pre, Brujah, 4)

(This is only 11 guys. Double up on two vampires you like, and remove
someone you don't. Personal preference: i would use two Rigby and two
Bianca, and remove Anvil.)

Library: (80 cards)
Master (10 cards)
5 Blood Doll
2 Celerity
2 Potence
1 Waste Management Operation

Action (19 cards)
7 Bum's Rush
6 Legal Manipulations
6 Social Charm

COMBAT: (51 cards)
Strike Cards (18)
6 Growing Fury
4 Mighty Grapple
8 Undead Strength

Support Cards (8)
4 Torn Signpost
4 Increased Strength

Celerity (25)
8 Acrobatics
5 Flash
4 Nimble Feet
4 Sideslip
4 Vampiric Speed

Tourist Information:
total presses (17)
total dodges (16)
additional strikes (12)

You'll notice that this doesn't look a damn bit like the traditional
Potence "beat their ass" deck, and has at least two cards that people
will froth over. There's a few reasons. First, the classic Potence
deck relies on increasing its hand damage with Torn Signpost or the
like and using Immortal Grapple (not easy cards to get). Second, I'm
assuming you'll HAVE to dodge their initial strike most of the time in
an intercept-combat environment, and so you have a bunch of Dodge.
Third, I'm leaning towards free cards so that you don't have to use
Taste of Vitae (also a difficult card to get).

Some of the advantages your metagame has given you: You don't have to
worry about S:CE or Dodge, so you can slide a little more into press
combat and be able to assume they'll stick around to get swatted - you
don't have to kill them on round 1 the way you normally would.
Because of this, you can use a lot more of the free dual-purpose
Celerity cards such as Vampiric Speed, and your Brujah/!Brujah will
have lots of superior Celerity for you. You can also mix and mismatch
most of the above cards/strikes well, since you're getting multiple
"start of rounds" where you can play TS/IS. And since you don't have
to worry about monster-fast bleed decks when everyone and their
grandmother is untapping and intercepting everything, you can go a bit
lighter on the Rush actions.

Presto, 80 card 0-stealth combat deck, and unless you're seeing a lot
of Fortitude, or non-strike damage such as Carrion Crows, you're in
pretty good shape. Even Fortitude will have trouble with the above,
though, because Skin of Steel doesn't deal well with press combat.

Actually, I'd also agree that Ravnos are potentially the best intercept clan.
Besides untap/intercept from Animalism, Chimerstry has two key cards: Ignis
Fatuus and Veiled Sight. Someone already noted they are blood intensive, but
the best part about them is that they reduce stealth (as opposed to increase
intercept).

So a Tzimisce may play a bunch of intercept cards, but that only affects him.
If he gets tapped or doesn't succeed, the other Tzimisce don't even have a
chance.

With Ignis Fatuus, every untapped Ravnos can play one. And Veiled Sight can
completely obliterate stealth (though you have to try to block).

And these cards can essentially provide intercept to other Methusaleh's
minions. If someone crosstable is calling a nasty vote, you can help provide
intercept (sort of like KRCG or London Evening Star), making them valuable
bargaining chips.
